name: Third Position
summary: Third Position is a post-war neo-fascist current that claims to transcend left and right by rejecting both capitalism and communism as materialist creeds. Its International Third Position form puts the primacy of the spirit and a return to the Christian faith first, and calls for a militant 'New Man' and worldwide National Revolution. It pairs distributist small ownership, guilds and hostility to usury and banks with racial separatism and repatriation, decentralised 'Popular Rule' bounded by God's law, and anti-Zionism.
scope: The neo-fascist Third Position as Berlet (s11) and the ECPS (s13) define it: the current that rejects both capitalism and communism, from Terza Posizione through the National Front's Political Soldier wing to the International Third Position. Malendowicz (s10) treats the ITP as its representative and names Derek Holland and Roberto Fiore as its ideologues and the ITP Declaration of Principles as its main document, so the answers rest on that Declaration (s8), Holland's Political Soldier (s9) and the movement's own statement of where it stands (s12). Excluded: the Argentine Peronist 'Third Position', which the ECPS treats separately; member parties' own platforms (Forza Nuova, National Rebirth of Poland) and American groups such as White Aryan Resistance, which are other subjects.

notes: Later pass (2026-11-09, rules 5): the first audit rested on Wikipedia, a press summary of Forza Nuova's 2009 programme and monitoring-group articles; its answers were re-sourced from the ITP Declaration of Principles, Holland's Political Soldier and the movement's statement, or nulled. Themes searched: economy and banking (Declaration points 8-9, statement), society and family (point 2), religion (points 1-3, 5), race and immigration (point 6), ecology (point 7), government and democracy (point 5, statement), world (points 4 and 10, statement: EU, NATO, UN), means (Holland on terrorism, means and ends). Technology, welfare, health, education and most foreign-policy specifics are not addressed. Forza Nuova's programme and the ITP's Final Conflict magazine (archive.org) were left out as one organisation's platform and campaign writing. Not reached: Lebourg's 'Ni droite, ni gauche: en avant!' on HAL refuses scripted access (bot check); Griffin's Nature of Fascism, Shaffer (2018) and Spektorowski (2003) are not open access; The Third Position Handbook (1997) was not found online.
